rationale: Rejected. It targets AI authorship, while the projects studied explicitly accept AI-assisted work and object to unreviewed, low-understanding work. The space is already crowded with low-adoption detectors.

Advanced to a cheap retrospective experiment. It addresses the best-evidenced problem, matches what the policies actually ask for (understanding, not abstinence), and its riskiest assumption can be tested with public data before any building.
Parked. Plausible, but it depends on network adoption, carries governance and abuse risk, and the incumbent (Vouch) could add federation itself. Revisit if cross-project list sharing emerges.
